title: Sitting in at the Sunset and copying Buster Bailey's solo
summary: He sat in at the Sunset Cafe and played Buster Bailey's 'Tootsie Goodbye' solo note for note, to Rudy Jackson's amusement; the band was Carroll Dickerson's.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: He really did. Yeah, I appreciate it. Funny thing about it, though, it was -- he was working with -- with this band down at the Sunset. So Simcan and I and Cecil Trwin Aaron, we all go and listen to the clarinet players, like Jimmy Noon, Buster Bailey and the different ones, you know. So Buster used to play this thing called Tod-Toot Tootsie Goodbye. Once he had -- I got it -- so bring him down to the Sunset, went in there, man, couple of guys, young fellows, and said, hey, Happy, come on and sit down. So Buster wasn't there that night. So I -- Rudy Jackson saxophone player, said, all right, Happy, said, come on and sit down. So I went and sat in -- so he played his thing, 'Tod-Toot Tootsie,' Goodbye.

I played the solo, exactly like in fact, Buster Bailey, said so Rudy said to me soon as he got set to leave, he said, 'hey, where did you get that like that?' I said 'because, I heard Buster play it over here a that note-for- couple times.' He said, 'how did you get all them multiple notes?' They went to (unintelligible) player said, 'oh, you're a copycat, huh?' And I said, 'no, I just like the way he played it did him all the good in the world, it.' He laughed and (unintelligible).
Which band was that then at -- Carroll
That was Carl Dickerson -- Carl Dickerson, uh-huh.
Carl Dickerson. They had some great bands (unintelligible). in Chicago at that time.
